thread.title: Wall Street Braces For Combative G7 Meeting

author: MT Newswires
title: Wall Street Braces For Combative G7 Meeting
text:
Shutterstock photo Panic-selling erupted overnight as worries over the outcome to this weekend's Group of Seven meeting coupled with the continued meltdown in emerging markets, soft Chinese and German economic data and selling pressure on Apple ( AAPL ) fueled investors' risk aversion, driving Dow futures as much as 100 points lower. While US futures are above their session lows, the major averages are all indicated to open in the red.
Investors are bracing for a contentious meeting between President Donald Trump and leaders of the EU, UK, Canada and Japan this weekend, all of which have come in the crosshairs of the president's trade agenda. Tensions were inflamed last night when Trump sent out a series of provocative tweets aimed at France and Canada in retaliation to their support of excluding the US from a joint G7 statement.
Emerging markets also weighed on global markets as recent rate hikes from Brazil and India and an emergency bailout loan of $50 billion to Argentina failed to soothe jittery investors. As a result, the MSCI emerging markets futures index is trading at its lowest level this year.
Finally, Apple shares are under attack and are set to trade lower for the first time in five days after the company reportedly told its suppliers to prepare for 20% fewer components for iPhones in the second half of 2018. Losses are weighing on the Nasdaq which is indicated to open nearly 1% lower on Friday.
Risk aversion has resulted in a weaker dollar against the yen and slightly lower Treasury yields, specifically in shorter-dated maturities. The 10-year Treasury note currently yields 2.92% versus 2.93% on Thursday.
Friday's economic calendar is light with only wholesale inventory and sales data at 10am ET and the weekly Baker Hughes rig count at 1pm ET.
